subject: System Design
title: HTTP/2 and Multiplexing
description: A 60-second lesson on HTTP/2 and Multiplexing.

hook.text: A web page loads 80 resources. With HTTP/1.1, the browser opens 6 connections and queues the rest.

buildup.text: HTTP/2 sends multiple requests over a single connection simultaneously using multiplexed streams.

discovery.text: Header compression and server push further reduce latency. Pages load noticeably faster.

twist.text: A single lost TCP packet blocks all streams — head-of-line blocking at the transport layer persists.

climax.text: HTTP/2 solved application-layer multiplexing but exposed TCP as the new bottleneck.

punchline.text: One connection, many streams — but TCP remains the limit.

quiz.question: What problem does HTTP/2 solve?
options: Multiple requests over a single connection via multiplexing
